subject: Civil Engineering
title: Liquefaction: When Soil Turns to Liquid
description: A micro-lesson that makes Liquefaction: When Soil Turns to Liquid usable.

hook.text: Solid ground turns to quicksand in seconds — buildings sink, tilt, and topple.

buildup.text: Loose, saturated sand loses all strength when shaken — water pressure pushes grains apart.

discovery.text: The soil behaves like a liquid — heavy structures sink while buried tanks float to the surface.

twist.text: Sand boils erupt — water and sand shoot up through cracks in the ground surface.

climax.text: Christchurch, New Zealand lost entire neighborhoods to liquefaction in 2011.

punchline.text: Solid ground is an illusion. Shake it hard enough and it flows like water.

quiz.question: What causes soil liquefaction during an earthquake?
options: Extreme heat from friction melts sand particles underground
Shaking increases water pressure in saturated sand, causing grains to lose contact and the soil to behave like liquid
Chemical reactions between water and minerals dissolve the soil structure
